summary: Rate-selector cache clear during region reroute caused loss of hourly buffer attribution and partial metering
description: Issue summary: During a cross-region failover window on 2026-03-11 22:40 UTC the rate-selector cache was cleared as part of a routable variant refresh. Impact: Several hourly buffer credits and a subset of hourly postbacks for NordicMaps were not attributed to the reserved-hour buffer bucket and instead landed as orphaned usage without buffer offsets. The customer reports a rise in provisional invoice line items (~$1,200) tied to warmup/warm-start tokens that should have been covered by the hourly buffer. Environment: Dedicated cluster (us-west), reserved-capacity org-nordicmaps, private rate-selector rollout v2.6.6. Observed at ~2026-03-11 22:45 UTC across ~20 minutes. Expected: Postbacks include rate_tag and hour_buffer attribution even under transient reroute/cache-refresh. Impact: Customer-facing billing variance, request for provisional credit and root-cause explanation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate region reroute by toggling routing-policy to 'prefer-eu' then back to 'prefer-us' during active warmup window.
2) Trigger a mixed multitenant microbatch (10k tokens) to cause postback emission across edge proxies.
3) Observe postback envelope in S3 /postbacks/ingest for missing rate_tag/hour_buffer fields and compare with normal postbacks.
4) Re-run postback reconciliation job; verify those postbacks are classified as 'unallocated' and do not consume hourly buffer credits.
logs: 2026-03-11T22:44:53Z rate-selector.INFO cache: invalidated key=routes:org-nordicmaps region=us-west trigger=rollout:v2.6.6
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 09:10 - Initial triage by Support (Priya): confirmed invoice variance and customer-provided sample postbacks.
2026-03-12 10:02 - SRE (Rafael) ran query against postback S3 manifest: found 732 postbacks from 22:40-23:05 UTC for org-nordicmaps with missing 'rate_tag' fields.

2026-03-12 11:20 - Correlated with infra rollout github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2854 which included a rate-selector cache clear to remove stale pinned variants during a canary-step. Rollout window matches missing postbacks timeframe.

Hypothesis: The cache clear removed in-memory routing metadata used to populate rate_tag/hour_buffer at the postback emission edge, causing postbacks to be emitted without rate attribution. When the reconciler ran it could not map those to hourly buffers, classifying them as unallocated usage.

Evidence: Postbacks show correct tokens/counts but missing 'rate_tag' and 'buffer_hour' fields. Metric postback_missing_rate_tag spiked from baseline 0.2/min to 28/min during the window. Reconciler logs show allocation_failed with 'no_hour_buffer_tag' for same ids.
customer_statement: 2026-03-12 08:42 - Lars Berg (NordicMaps): 'We see a $1.2k provisional charge on our dashboard for warm-start usage that should be covered by our hourly buffer. Please advise — this occurred during our peak run.'
Customer requests: provisional credit for affected hour, confirmation that future reroutes won't lose buffer attribution, and a replay/backfill of postbacks if possible.
actions_taken: 2026-03-12 12:05 - Support acknowledged and escalated to SRE and Billing. (Priya)
2026-03-12 13:40 - SRE stopped the live cache-clear action on in-flight rollouts and added a short-circuit to preserve rate_tag until postback emission completes. Temporary mitigation in place.
2026-03-12 15:15 - Billing prepared provisional credit template and requested list of postback ids for reconciliation.

2026-03-13 09:00 - Reconciler backfill job planned: will attempt to reprocess S3 postbacks to re-attach rate_tag using routing history and then re-run allocation. Backfill dry-run found ~615 postbacks re-assignable to hourly buffer.
resolution: Workaround: We applied a short-term guard so rate-selector cache clears do not remove routing metadata for in-flight requests. Backfill plan: reconciler will reprocess 615 of the 732 missing postbacks and reassign hourly buffer credits; billing will apply a provisional credit of $1,200 pending final backfill results. Permanent fix: PR github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2867 (rate-selector: persist routing snapshot to postback envelope on reroute) merged and scheduled for 2026-03-16 canary. Customer notified and provisional credit applied on 2026-03-14. Follow-up: monitor postback_missing_rate_tag metric for 7 days and confirm no further regressions.
next_steps: 1) Run backfill to reassign hourly buffer credits and update invoices (owner: Billing, target: 2026-03-14).
2) Deploy PR 2867 to canary and validate with synthetic reroute tests (owner: Infra, target: 2026-03-16).
3) Keep customer updated via daily status until resolved (owner: Support).
4) Postmortem doc linking to confluence and runbook updates (owner: SRE & Billing).
